q: What does HSN stand for?
exp: Developed by the World Customs Organization, used in over 200 countries.

q: What's SAC in GST?
exp: SAC codes classify services and start with 99.

q: All SAC codes for services start with which digits?
exp: Chapter 99 covers services, e.g. 9983 for other professional and technical services.

q: How many digits does the Indian HSN (as used in customs tariff) go up to?
exp: The first 6 are internationally harmonised; India adds 2 more for national detail.

q: Custom software development services generally fall under SAC:
exp: 9954 is construction, 9971 financial services, 9965 goods transport.

q: SAC 9963 covers:
exp: Hotels and restaurants fall here.

q: SAC 9965 covers:
exp: GTA services, freight and so on.

q: Pre-packaged 'canned' software sold as a licence is generally classified as:
options: Goods under HSN 8523 or as a service under 9973/9984 depending on the mode
exp: Software is a classic grey area. Both routes attract 18%, so the practical impact is mostly on place of supply and documentation.

q: How many HSN digits must a business with AATO up to ₹5 crore mention on B2B tax invoices?
exp: Optional for B2C invoices.

q: How many HSN digits must a business with AATO above ₹5 crore mention on all tax invoices?
exp: This applies to both B2B and B2C.

q: In GSTR-1, the HSN summary in Table 12 has, since 2025, been reported:
options: Separately for B2B and B2C supplies, with HSN chosen from a dropdown
exp: This was rolled out in phases from early 2025.

q: The HSN code on an e-invoice is validated against the GST master list, so an invalid HSN is rejected by the IRP.
exp: IRPs validate HSN codes against the master.

q: How many General Rules for Interpretation (GRI) guide HSN classification?
exp: GRI 1 to 6, used for goods classification.

q: Under GRI 1, classification is first determined by:
options: The terms of the headings and section or chapter notes
exp: Titles of sections and chapters are only for reference.

q: When goods could be classified under two headings, GRI 3(a) says prefer the heading with:
exp: If that doesn't settle it, 3(b) looks at essential character, and 3(c) takes the heading that occurs last in numerical order.

q: A kit of different items packed for retail sale is classified under GRI 3(b) based on:
options: The item that gives the set its essential character
exp: E.g. a hair-cutting kit is classified as the clippers.

q: Who decides classification disputes for a specific taxpayer in advance?
exp: The ruling binds only the applicant and its jurisdictional officer.

q: Which body recommends GST rate changes?
options: The GST Council, after which rates are notified by the government
exp: Rate notifications for goods and services are issued by CBIC.

q: Which notification originally set out GST rates for goods?
exp: 11/2017 is for services rates, 2/2017 for goods exemptions, 12/2017 for services exemptions. Amended many times since.

q: After the September 2025 changes, standalone restaurant services (outside hotels with high room tariffs) are taxed at:
exp: Restaurants in 'specified premises' (hotels with room tariff above ₹7,500) pay 18% with ITC.

q: Hotel accommodation with a tariff up to ₹7,500 per night, after September 2025, is taxed at:
exp: It was 12% with ITC before the rationalisation.

q: Items like air-conditioners and televisions (above 32 inches) moved in September 2025 from:
exp: Most 28% items moved to 18%; a narrow set of luxury and sin goods went to 40%.

q: Sale of a ready-to-move flat with a completion certificate attracts:
exp: Under-construction flats: 1% for affordable housing and 5% for others, without ITC.

q: Coaching classes (not a recognised school) are taxed at:
exp: Services by recognised educational institutions up to higher secondary are exempt, but private coaching isn't.

q: A company sells a gift box containing a steel water bottle (18%) and a packet of dry fruits (5%) for one price. What rate applies, and how would you set it up in billing software?
model: The items aren't naturally bundled, so it's a mixed supply taxed at the highest rate among the items: 18% on the whole price. In software, either create the gift box as a separate SKU with its own HSN (the highest-rate item's classification) and 18%, or bill items separately with their own prices and rates to avoid mixed supply. The second option usually lowers tax if prices are genuinely separate.
points: Highest rate applies to entire value
exp: How a product is packaged and priced can change its tax.

q: A client with ₹8 crore turnover prints 4-digit HSN codes on B2B invoices. What's the issue?
options: Above ₹5 crore, 6-digit HSN is required on invoices and in GSTR-1
exp: Validation on the portal and IRP increasingly enforces digit counts.
